### Observed differences

- The clearest difference lies in the order among A11, A12 and A13. In the earlier window, A11 was followed by A13 in about 52 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (A12 about 22, A14 about 24), A13 led back to A12 in about 44 of 100 (A11 about 20), and A12 went to A14 (about 39) or A11 (about 37) far more often than to A13 (about 20). In the later window, A11's most frequent successor is A12 (about 41 of 100, with A13 down to about 26), A13 returns to A11 in about 32 of 100 (A12 about 31), and A12 goes to A13, A11 and A14 in nearly equal shares (about 32–33 each). The dominant sequence A11→A13→A12 thus gave way to a mixed order in which the reverse sequence A11→A12→A13 is at least as frequent. [DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]
- This is a re-weighting of existing transitions rather than activities appearing or disappearing: A11, A12 and A13 each occur in about 45–49 of 100 traces in both windows. The inflow into this fragment shifted consistently: A03 now leads to A13 in about 37 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 27 before) and to A11 in about 31 (about 39 before). [OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, DIR003]
- A43 and A42 are executed and repeated more often in the later window: A43 appears in about 51 of 100 traces versus about 44 before and, when present, recurs more often (mean occurrences per trace about 0.71→0.87; recurrence in about 21.5 of 100 traces versus 16); A42 rises from about 16.5 to 23 of 100 traces. [OCC036, OCC035]
- In another branch, A19 and A23 participate more often (about 47→53.5 and 46.5→53.5 of 100 traces) while A20, A24 and A18 participate less often (about 55→47.5, 53.5→47 and 32.5→26.5); the successor shares move the same way: A44 now passes to A19 in about 49 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 43.5 before) and to A20 in about 42 (about 52 before), A24 passes to A21 in about 32 (about 18.5 before), A22 passes to A24 in about 20 (about 32 before), and A30 passes to A23 in about 28 (about 21 before). [OCC017, OCC021, OCC018, OCC022, OCC016, DIR044, DIR024, DIR022, DIR030]
- A few activities that occur in every trace now also repeat occasionally: A44 and A50 recur in about 3 of 100 traces (previously never and about 0.5), and A25 in about 1.5 of 100; A50's observed outgoing transitions also rise from 5 to 22 and spread over many more targets, though these proportions rest on very few observations. [OCC037, OCC042, OCC023, DIR050]
- Rare activities became somewhat more visible: A08 appears in about 10.5 of 100 traces versus about 4 before (21 versus 8 traces), with its outgoing transitions redistributed across many targets, and A04 rises from about 7 to 10 of 100 traces (20 versus 14 traces); both rest on few observations. [OCC008, DIR008, OCC004]
- Two further regions reroute moderately between existing successors: around A31 and A37–A40 (A39→A40 up from about 45 to 55 of 100 with A39→A32 down from about 48 to 39; A37→A32 up and A37→A38 down; A38→A37 up from about 45 to 55; A31→A39 up from about 23 to 30 with A31→A37 down from about 27 to 20), and around A25/A35/A36 (A25→A35 up from about 30 to 38 with A25→A41 down from about 36 to 27; A35→A41 up from about 30 to 38; A36→A27 up from about 30 to 36 with A36→A35 down from about 34 to 26). [DIR039, DIR037, DIR038, DIR031, DIR025, DIR035, DIR036]
- Around A01/A05/A07/A09 the shares between existing successors also shifted: A01 passes to A05 less often (about 37→25 of 100) and to A09 more often (about 27→35); A07 passes to A05 more often (about 29→42) and to A09 less often (about 34→22); A05 passes to A14 more often (about 26→34) and to A07 less often (about 37→28). [DIR001, DIR007, DIR005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the ordering between A11, A12 and A13 changed: in the earlier window their flow mostly ran along the sequence A11→A13→A12 (A11→A13 in about 52 of 100 of A11's outgoing transitions, A13→A12 about 44), whereas in the later window that sequence weakened (to about 26 and 31) and the reverse sequence A11→A12→A13→A11 became about as frequent (about 41, 33 and 32 of 100), leaving no fixed order between the three. All three activities already occurred in about 45–49 of 100 traces in both windows, so existing paths are taken with different frequencies rather than activities being added or removed; the change is shown directly and coherently by the successor distributions of A11, A12 and A13 themselves, each difference being larger than in roughly 174–199 of 200 random re-splits, and the increased inflow A03→A13 (about 27→37 of 100) fits the same picture. The evidence cannot rule out that a shift in the mix of cases reaching this fragment, rather than a local change in the ordering rule, produces the same successor shares; the evidence also covers only control-flow occurrence and direct succession and includes no baseline for how many items an unchanged process would flag. [DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, DIR003, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013]

Other differences:

- A43 and A42 are executed and repeated more often (A43: about 44→51 of 100 traces, mean occurrences per trace about 0.71→0.87, recurrence about 16→21.5 of 100; A42: about 16.5→23 of 100 traces). [OCC036, OCC035]
- A19 and A23 participate more often while A20, A24 and A18 participate less often, with matching successor shifts at A44 (toward A19, away from A20), A24 (toward A21), A22 and A30. [OCC017, OCC021, OCC018, OCC022, OCC016, DIR044, DIR024, DIR022, DIR030]
- A44, A50 and A25, previously executed about once per trace, now repeat in roughly 1.5–3 of 100 traces. [OCC037, OCC042, OCC023]
- The rare activities A08 (about 4→10.5 of 100 traces) and A04 (about 7→10) appear in more traces, though on only 8–21 supporting traces each. [OCC008, OCC004, DIR008]
- Moderate rerouting between existing successors around A31/A37–A40, A25/A35/A36 and A01/A05/A07/A09. [DIR039, DIR037, DIR038, DIR031, DIR025, DIR035, DIR036, DIR001, DIR007, DIR005]
